solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greatest foreign character, in principle

indicators.note: one piece is set inside the other, so the Greek letter sits within the word for a principle

parts.note: a maxim is a guiding principle or rule
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign character

explanation.surface: Someone asserting, in principle, that a foreigner has the best character.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximum used as an adjective means the largest or highest possible, hence greatest.

clue.text: Humble carers taking lowest income

parts.note: mean can mean humble or lowly, as in of mean birth

indicators.note: in a down clue the lowest letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: Carers on minimum wage with modest earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's means are their financial resources, the money they live on.

clue.text: This repeatedly makes a female kiss and smooch more animatedly

parts.note: X is the symbol for a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: acting animatedly means moving in a lively way, so the letters of smooch and more are stirred up

explanation.surface: A romantic scene where kissing grows ever more lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animatedly' rearranges SMOOCH with the word 'more', which reads in the surface as a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Two copies of the X chromosome give a female in humans, hence repeated it produces one.

clue.text: After changing top from small to medium, dupes mates

indicators.note: the top letter of a down entry is its first, swapped from one letter to another
to marks the replacement letter that the first letter of the dupes word becomes

parts.note: suckers are dupes, people easily fooled
S is the abbreviation for small in clothing sizes
M is the abbreviation for medium in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A clothes-shop swap of size labels that fools one's friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Muckers is British slang for close friends or pals.

clue.text: Right to stop girls chasing £500 — they'll turn nuts

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the girls come after the money

parts.note: monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so the letter goes inside the word for girls

parts.note: wenches is an old word for girls or young women

explanation.surface: A rich man paying girls to stop him, though they are going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey wrenches are adjustable spanners used to turn nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Chance magistrate will crush resistance

indicators.note: to crush something is to squeeze it, here held inside the magistrate

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A defendant's opportunity arrives because the magistrate will stamp out opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAK is British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is a lucky opportunity, as in 'give me a break'.

clue.text: Cake placed on earthenware in Japanese theatre

indicators.note: in a down entry, placed on means sitting above, so the cake comes first

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
raku is a Japanese lead-glazed earthenware

explanation.surface: A snack served on a pottery plate at a Japanese performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunraku is the traditional Japanese puppet theatre form.

clue.text: The last things you'd see in the cow pasture — would include me

definitions.text: The last things you'd see in the cow pasture — would include me

indicators.note: the last things of these words are their final letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A sheep remarking that it would be among the final sights in a cow field.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of 'The', 'cow' and 'pasture' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it: a ewe could graze in that pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, an animal found grazing in fields alongside cattle.

clue.text: Vulgar jerk ultimately restless about son

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word jerk
about means surrounding, so the word for restless goes round the letter for son

parts.note: itchy means restless or fidgety, as in itchy feet

explanation.surface: A crude, impatient man fussing over his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitschy describes garish, tasteless art or decor, so vulgar in the sense of lacking taste.

clue.text: In came finalist, playing this rag

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters of the phrase are moved around

explanation.surface: A sports report: in came a finalist, playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this rag' points to the paper the puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is slang for a newspaper, and this crossword appears in the Financial Times.

clue.text: It's been burnt when hot

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Something has been scorched while it was hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue left after a material has been burnt.

clue.text: Engineer sent unopened incoming goods for dispatch

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters that follow are rearranged
not opened means without its first letter, so the word loses its opening

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange for incoming goods to be sent on without being unpacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' strips the I from 'incoming' to leave NCOMING; 'Engineer' rearranges that with SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment is a batch of goods delivered or sent off to a recipient.

clue.text: My southern accent, oddly meek

parts.note: an accent is a tone of voice

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word meek

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that their Southern way of speaking sounds strangely timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone me is a British exclamation of astonishment, just as 'My!' is.

clue.text: Anything but bloody American baroque cinema

indicators.note: baroque means extravagantly ornate and distorted, so the word cinema is twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A film critic insisting that American art-house cinema is never gory.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic means lacking blood, so pale and the opposite of full-blooded.

clue.text: Machine-powered muscle finally yielded and split

parts.note: muscle is the body's motor, the thing that produces movement

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word yielded

parts.note: riven means split or torn apart

explanation.surface: A strained muscle that eventually gave way and tore.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor-driven means operated by an engine rather than by hand.

clue.text: US Homeland broadcast boring criminal drug tycoon

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so sown

explanation.surface: A US TV show broadcasts a dull drama about a criminal drugs baron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like the anagram signal but means sowed; 'criminal' scrambles the drug tycoon, and 'boring' drills the sowing word into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: God's own country is a nickname for the United States, viewed as a blessed homeland.

clue.text: Recipient of charge after attack on drunken toerags

indicators.note: the word for attack comes after the jumbled piece
drunks stagger about, so the letters of toerags are jumbled

parts.note: battery is an attack, as in assault and battery

explanation.surface: A police report of an assault by inebriated yobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges TOERAGS to STORAGE. A toerag is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A storage battery is an accumulator, which takes in electric charge and holds it.

clue.text: Concede after quarrel in Bath, say

indicators.note: the word for concede comes after the quarrel

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
to own, as in own up, is to admit or concede

explanation.surface: Giving way after a domestic row in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is the English city, not a tub; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is a famous English spa town, known for its Roman hot springs.

clue.text: Not in favour of entertaining forward old merchant

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: anti means against or not in favour of
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Opposed to hosting a pushy old trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Tense doctor in row over thread? Sort of

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, the doctor within the turned row
in a down clue, over means the word for row is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: An anxious doctor in an argument over a thread of discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means read upwards, so the row word reverses; 'in' sets the doctor within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a thin, thread-like coiling shoot that a climbing plant uses for support.

clue.text: First day of month gripped by a cold — not if this

indicators.note: being gripped means held within, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the first of September can be written SEPT I

explanation.surface: A warning that on the first of the month you'll be stuck with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: SEPT I sits between A and C. The definition reads back through the clue: you would not catch a cold if you were this.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from infection-causing germs, so a sterile person would not pick up a cold.

clue.text: Fly back stuff — it's a puzzle

indicators.note: back means the insect's name is read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
to ram is to cram or stuff

explanation.surface: An angler's tackle advice ending in confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven pieces forming shapes.

clue.text: Dull, hard, second subject

parts.note: mat (or matt) means dull, not glossy
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A pupil's verdict on a tedious, difficult school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Maths is a school subject, the British short form of mathematics.

clue.text: Scientist's mobile phone empire

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so these letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: A researcher owns a mobile phone business empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Oppenheimer was the physicist who led the Manhattan Project.

clue.text: Go with power base, suppressing pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry suppressing means sitting on top of, so the base comes above pressure

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
e is the base of natural logarithms
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Advice to proceed with a power base while keeping down any pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means energy or vigour, as in full of go, which is what pep is.

clue.text: Examine old soldier

definitions.meaning: short for veteran, a former soldier

explanation.surface: Inspect a war veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: Vet means to check carefully, and in US use it is short for veteran.

clue.text: Finished by noon, article mostly lacking

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter, so the word for lacking is cut short

parts.note: poor means lacking, as in poor in resources

explanation.surface: A job done by midday, though an article was largely missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the R from POOR to leave POO.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoo is First World War British slang meaning done for or used up.

clue.text: Strips spelling courses

parts.note: lines are courses or routes, as in lines of action

explanation.surface: A school timetable dropping its spelling lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strips' is a noun, not the verb it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Splines are thin flexible strips of wood or metal, or slats fitted into grooves.
